subject: Sizing questions and deployment decision checklist — reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finosys.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing questions and deployment decision checklist — reserved GPUs

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying questions so we can produce a conservative Dedicated sizing recommendation (and pricing). I pasted the items below and attached a one-page workbook to fill in if that’s easier.

Call highlights (my notes):
- You’re targeting LLM-powered chat for customer support triage initially, with eventual expansion to contextual search and embeddings workflows for product recommendations.
- Preference is to land on Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable latency and data residency, but you’re open to a brief Hosted pilot during ramp.
- SLA sensitivity: p95 latency target ~ <250ms for short exchanges; throughput needs spike during business hours.

Follow-ups / clarifications we need to size properly:
1) Target sustained TPS (requests/sec) and peak TPS during hour-long peaks. Please indicate both.
2) Average and 95th-percentile token mix: average user request tokens in, and expected generation tokens out (e.g., 30 | 80).
3) Concurrent sessions (avg and peak) — how many simultaneous active chats do you expect?
4) Embeddings volume: are you serving real-time embedding requests per chat, or running background batch jobs for indexing? Please give approximate QPS or batch size/minute.
5) Data residency / VPC needs: you mentioned eventual VPC. Timeline? Do you need Private (customer-managed control plane) from day one?
6) Any hard requirement on GPU family (A100 vs H100) or a budget constraint we should respect?
7) Expected go-live date and ramp profile (linear, step, or staged pilots).

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the attached reserved_capacity_workbook.xlsx (short worksheet) and return it — that will let us compute candidate pools (gpu count + SKU) and expected unit cost.
- We’ll model two options: H100-optimized low-latency pool, and an A100-cost-optimized pool with slightly higher latency but lower $/token.
- Quick follow-up call mid-next-week to walk through the workbook and our recommended SOW outline.

Attachments: reserved_capacity_workbook.xlsx (xlsx) — small worksheet; redwood_capacity_notes.pdf (pdf) — short explainer on GPU tradeoffs and batching.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the follow-up after I get the workbook back.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finosys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finosys Procurement <procure@finosys.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing questions and deployment decision checklist — reserved GPUs

Hi Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Answers below inline.

1) TPS: Sustained 80 TPS across our support funnels; expected peak ~220 TPS during hour-long morning spikes. (Peaks are predictable around 10–11am PT).
2) Token mix: Avg request tokens in ~25; avg generation tokens out ~60. For 95th percentile, plan for 120 tokens total.
3) Concurrent sessions: Avg concurrent active sessions ~420; peak concurrent ~1,100.
4) Embeddings: Two parts — (a) real-time per-conversation embeddings ~0.5 QPS during steady-state (bursty during onboarding) and (b) nightly batch index update ~50k vectors per hour.
5) Data residency/VPC: We will require VPC for production in Q3; for the initial pilot in June we can use Dedicated in your hosted control plane (no Private deployment Day 1).
6) GPU family: No hard mandate. Procurement prefers A100-series due to cost profile, but our ML team favors H100 if the latency delta is meaningful. Please show both configurations.
7) Go-live: Pilot early June (4-week pilot), then production ramp in August with full traffic by late September if pilot looks good.

Budget: procurement asked for a preliminary $/month banding for each configuration so they can assess. They will also need a short procurement checklist if we choose Dedicated (e.g., SOC 2 evidence, network peering requirements).

Thanks — I’ll ask procurement to review the workbook once you return it.

Best,
Laura Chen
VP, Product Operations — Finosys
laura.chen@finosys.com

Laura — great, this is exactly what we needed, thanks for the fast turnaround. A few quick notes based on your answers and internal sizing guidance (copied Aditya and Lauren for infra/solutions input):

- Given the 220 TPS peak and ~1,100 peak concurrency, our initial sizing window will model a 2-cluster approach:
  * Primary low-latency cluster (H100) sized for 70% of peak interactive requests to hold p95 <250ms for short chat exchanges.
  * Secondary cost-optimized cluster (A100) handling background batch work and overflow (embeddings indexing + burst overflow).

- Token mix suggests reasonable KV cache and batching opportunities: we’ll assume an average sequence length of 85 tokens for pipeline sizing and model memory estimates.

- Embeddings: we recommend separating online real-time embedding endpoint (small pool on A100) from large nightly batch workers to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

Action items / next steps:
1) Aditya will take your workbook and run two concrete SKU simulations — H100-heavy (latency-focused) and A100-heavy (cost-focused) — and provide GPU count, expected p95 latency, and estimated $/hour per cluster. (Aditya: can you target EOD Thu?)
2) Lauren will assemble a short procurement checklist for Dedicated (SOC 2 artifacts, expected peering requirements, and contract lead times).
3) Marissa & Laura — follow-up 30-min sync on Thu to review the worksheet outputs and procurement checklist. I’ll send a calendar invite if that time works.

Attachments re-sent: reserved_capacity_workbook.xlsx; redwood_capacity_notes.pdf
Related: draft SOW link — https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/FS-2027-0564-capacity

Thanks all — if procurement needs a simple line-item $/month band now, I can provide a conservative estimate by tomorrow morning.
